guide.title: Anub'arak's Overview
guide.text:
Anub'arak is an aggressive anti-caster Tank. His strongest points are his
long-range disruption and powerful on-demand resistance to Ability-based
damage. Although considered an archetypal Tank, Anub'arak's
Health pool is considerably lower than that of other Tanks. He relies on
opportunism and teamwork to survive, exemplifying the adage "the best defence is
a good offence."

guide.title: Anub'arak's Strengths and Weaknesses
guide.text:
Strengths
Excellent initiator
Access to Cocoon, a valuable Heroic Ability
Several long-range interruption Abilities
Weaknesses
Fragile for a Tank
Limited damage output and waveclear
Main Abilities are skillshots that can be avoided

guide.title: Anub'arak's Synergies and Counters
guide.text:
Anub'arak synergizes with
Anub'arak's aggressive crowd control-oriented Ability set makes him
particularly useful to any Hero who is able to follow up on said
crowd control with their own Ability combo.
Anub'arak is countered by
Anub'arak's aggressive game plan is difficult to execute against Heroes that
have ways of avoiding his skillshot or becoming immune to
crowd control on-demand.

guide.title: Anub'arak's Maps
guide.text:
Anub'arak's stronger maps
Anub'arak's average maps
Anub'arak's weaker maps
Anub'arak can be played without major issues on most Maps
because he has access to powerful engage
and peeling tools.
His best Map is Alterac Pass because,
by using his Trait to keep Guards busy, he can capture the enemy Objective
all by himself as long as the enemy Heroes are busy somewhere else.
Maps where aggressive plays are rewarded (notably Dragon Shire)
are great for Anub'arak because, when the enemy team is split into small groups,
he can make high-risk high-reward plays to gain an advantage.
He does not excel on Maps where the Tank
has to posture in vision for long (for example Braxis Holdout)
because Anub'arak is not that durable against Basic Attacks
or where those Heroes are popular.

guide.title: Anub'arak's Tips and Tricks
guide.text:
Burrow Charge is your only way out, so you should choose wisely when to use it aggressively.
Impale is your primary engage tool but it can also be used for peeling.
Try to hold Harden Carapace for when you will be hit by enemy Abilities.
Exploit Scarab Host Beetles to gain vision, intercept skillshots, or tank Structures and Mercenaries (especially Bosses).
Use Locust Swarm before your Health becomes too low because the healing it provides is not instant.
Be creative with Cocoon: use it to setup engages or to isolate powerful enemy Heroes.
See our Abilities page for further information »

guide.title: Anub'arak's Role in the Current Meta
guide.text:
Anub'arak is a unique Tank that sacrifices raw durability
for powerful on-demand initiations. In general, Anub'arak players are
expected to look for opportunities to lock down isolated targets (through
Impale and Burrow Charge)
to allow their teammates to follow up.
In the early stages of the game, Anub'arak is well-suited for roaming
and protecting teammates in lanes. Burrow Charge lets him effectively scout
with very little danger. This task is just as important as initiating throughout
the entire game. As Heroic Abilities become available, Cocoon is the
expected choice to catch and aggressively collapse on rotating opponents
on top of being generally useful.

abilities.title: Anub'arak's Tips and Tricks
abilities.text:
Burrow Charge is your only way out, so you should choose wisely when to use it aggressively.
Impale is your primary engage tool but it can also be used for peeling.
Try to hold Harden Carapace for when you will be hit by enemy Abilities.
Exploit Scarab Host Beetles to gain vision, intercept skillshots, or tank Structures and Mercenaries (especially Bosses).
Use Locust Swarm before your Health becomes too low because the healing it provides is not instant.
Be creative with Cocoon: use it to setup engages or to isolate powerful enemy Heroes.

abilities.title: Impale
abilities.text:
Impale
(Q)
Anub'arak
Mana: 65
Cooldown: 12 seconds
Deals 90 (+4% per level) damage. Stuns for 1 second.
Impale provides a long-range area of effect Stun
to initiate and peel. Its range
makes it an excellent tool to interrupt
channeled Abilities.
Due to its relatively slow traveling speed comared to other skillshots,
Impale can easily hit foes that are near you, but enemies located at
maximum range will have more time to evade it due to the spikes' traveling
time. With some practice, however, it becomes easier to successfully predict
enemy movement and land hits with Impale.
As with most crowd control Abilities, Impale
has a long cooldown and does little damage of its own. This makes it a poor
waveclearing Ability, so it is better to find opportunities to
use it against Heroes (for example by ganking), but make sure you have
allied Heroes nearby to follow up on the Stun it provides.

abilities.title: Burrow Charge
abilities.text:
Burrow Charge
(E)
Anub'arak
Mana: 65
Cooldown: 14 seconds
Burrow to the target location, dealing 91 (+4% per level) damage and briefly stunning enemies in a small area upon surfacing, slowing them by 25% for 2.5 seconds.
Burrow Charge can be reactivated to surface early.
Burrow Charge provides Anub'arak with long-range
mobility, a short Stun to interrupt
channeled Abilities, as well as a
moderate Slow.
Thanks to its fast speed and
collisionless nature, it is the perfect tool with
which to initiate fights, catch up to fleeing Heroes,
or escape. When initiating,
always try and surface (by recasting the Burrow Charge while Anubarak is
underground) in the direction your intended target may be trying to move in.
This will put you in a position where you will be able to perform
body-blocking maneuvers.
When you want to engage without putting yourself at risk,
you should start with Impale
and then decide if you want to follow-up with
Burrow Charge or keep it to escape.
When you want to dive with your team, you can use them in the
opposite order. Do not dive alone.
Burrow Charge's long range can be advantageous or disadvantageous: although
it lets you catch opponents by surprise, it can also lead you to
overextend out of your teammate's range, preventing
them from properly follow up or assisting you. Be
sure to account for your allies' positioning when aggressively using Burrow
Charge.

abilities.title: Harden Carapace
abilities.text:
Harden Carapace
(W)
Anub'arak
Mana: 25
Cooldown: 7 seconds
Gain a Shield that grants 40 Spell Armor and absorbs 340 (+4% per level) damage over 3 seconds.
Harden Carapace is a key Basic Ability in making up for
Anub'arak's limited Health pool. Although the Shield provided is not that big,
the amount of Spell Armor provided can absorb
a huge amount of damage if used at the right time. As such, it is preferable
to use it when we expect enemy Heroes to use their offensive Abilities
or right before we get crowd controlled.

abilities.title: Locust Swarm
abilities.text:
In this section we discuss how this Heroic Ability works and give some tips on how to use it.
If you are looking for a detailed explanation on when and why you should pick it,
check out the dedicated section in the Talent Build page.
Locust Swarm
(R)
Anub'arak
Heroic
Mana: 75
Cooldown: 100 seconds
Deal 68 (+4% per level) damage per second to nearby enemies. Each enemy damaged restores 24 (+4% per level) Health. Lasts 6 seconds.
Besides the fact that Locust Swarm deals an
appreciable amount of area of effect damage, this Ability makes Anub'arak
harder to kill without a concerted effort from your opponents due
to its significant self-healing component. That said, it is barely useful
against burst damage.
Locust Swarm takes into account all
enemy entities—including Minions, Summons, Structures, and, of course,
Heroes—for the purpose of Health gains, making it especially effective
against grouped enemies. Due to its long cooldown, it is advised to only
use it in team fights, when the extra survivability comes in handy to stay alive.
Using such a long cooldown for ganking is generally a waste.

abilities.title: Cocoon
abilities.text:
In this section we discuss how this Heroic Ability works and give some tips on how to use it.
If you are looking for a detailed explanation on when and why you should pick it,
check out the dedicated section in the Talent Build page.
Cocoon
(R)
Anub'arak
Heroic
Mana: 70
Cooldown: 70 seconds
Wraps target enemy Hero in a cocoon, rendering them unable to act or be targeted for 7 seconds. Allies of the Hero can attack the cocoon to break it and free them early.
Cocoon is a unique Ability that is primarily used
to instantly take specific Heroes out of the game for a lengthy time period,
preventing them from using key Abilities. Do not use it on Heroes who can
instantly become Unstoppable (for example
Johanna via Iron Skin)
or enter Stasis (such as Maiev
via Vault of the Wardens)
without Stunning them beforehand.
During team fights, isolating Abilities like Cocoon are typically
used to disable Healers with powerful healing
Abilities (such as Alexstrasza). This forces their teammates to then
decide between keeping fighting without their presence or wasting resources
to free them.
Sometimes, however, you want to use Cocoon
on Heroes who can deal a tremendous amount of damage (for example Tassadar
with Archon). Cho'Gall,
being two Heroes in one, is the best target for Cocoon.
Cocoon is also an excellent tool for holding lone Heroes in place while your
nearby teammates collapse on them. Cocoon can be used in this manner to great
effect during the rotational phases that many of the
Maps call for, netting your team easy kills that would otherwise be very
difficult to get.
Cocoon's instant crowd control
effect can also allow you or your teammates to escape otherwise deadly
situations, preferably while trading it
with another Heroic Ability with a similar or longer cooldown.
Cocoon's remaining duration is clearly indicated by a green bar found
just above the Cocoon itself. You or your teammates can prepare your Abilities
for when the target is to be released from the Cocoon, as to
follow up rightly, however, enemy Heroes can damage
the Cocoon to open it sooner. You can use
Impale just as the Cocoon expires to secure a Stun
to prevent your target from using Abilities that may help them escape.

abilities.title: Scarab Host
abilities.text:
Scarab Host
(D)
Anub'arak
Cooldown: 8 seconds
Using an Ability spawns a Beetle which loses Health over 10 seconds, attacking nearby enemies for 20 (+4% per level) damage.
The Beetles spawned through Scarab Host are an
integral yet subtle part of Anub'arak's playstyle. Individual Beetles each add
approximately 20% more damage to Anub'arak's Basic Attacks, which rapidly adds
up as Anub'arak can consistently be surrounded by one to five of them.
Defensively, Beetles also act as extra bodies to catch single-target
skillshots (for example Storm Bolt
by Muradin before he gets enough stacks for it to pierce),
indirectly increasing Anub'arak's and his allies' survivability. They also do a
good job of tanking Minions, Structures, Mercenaries, and other things that
would otherwise attack Anub'arak himself.
Harden Carapace can be used to spawn
Beetles cheaply and on demand, even when you do not actually need to Shield
yourself. This is useful when doing Bosses as you can use Beetles to
drastically reduce them damage they deal to you: spawn a Beetle,
step back so it takes aggro, attack the Boss, and repeat.

talent_pages.text:

Nerubian Armor
(Level 1)
Anub'arak
Increase Harden Carapace's Spell Armor by 25.
Nerubian Armor is a good Talent that
increases the Spell Armor coming from
Harden Carapace, making Anub'arak extremely hard
to kill with Abilities.
Even against Heroes that do not rely on Abilities
as their main damage source, Nerubian Armor
will still give a good amount of value, especially in the early game.

Legion of Beetles
(Level 1)
Anub'arak
Beetles have 30 Spell Armor. Automatically spawn a Beetle every 12 seconds. Can be toggled on and off.
Legion of Beetles is a good Talent that
improves your ability to intercept enemy skillshot
directed towards you or allied Heroes by making Beetles harder to kill.
You also get an additional Beetle, slightly increasing your damage output.
When playing this Talent, you should toggle it off when mounted,
so that you do not end up wasting its effect when randomly being dismounted,
or before using Burrow Charge, because Beetles
spawn at the starting location. If you do not waste it, you will also
have it ready for checking bushes.
You can further increase the damage provided by this Talent
by combining it with Leeching Scarabs at Level 7,
Burning Beetles at Level 13,
and optionally with Beetle, Juiced at Level 16.

(Level 1)
Anub'arak
Quest: Gathering a Regeneration Globe increases your Health Regeneration by 1 per second, up to 30.
Reward: After gathering 25 Regeneration Globes, you also gain 500 Health.
Regeneration Master is a situational Talent that
increases your Health Regeneration and, after completing its Quest
in the late game, your maximum Health.
You should consider picking this Talent when most of the damage done by enemy Heroes
will be in the form of Basic Attacks because Nerubian Armor
does nothing against Physical Damage and
Legion of Beetles can only block skillshots.
The best Maps for collecting many Regeneration Globes are:
Alterac Pass
Blackheart's Bay
Dragon Shire

Anub'arak
Create a bed of spikes along Impale's path that Slows enemies by 25% and deals 21 (+4% per level) damage per second. Spikes persist for 3.5 seconds.
Bed of Barbs is a good Talent that
improves Impale by adding a respectable
area of effect
Slow to it.
Beetles, generated via Scarab Host,
move at 4 units per second. Heroes are a bit faster, so the Slow
you get from this Talent can help them stick on enemy Heroes,
so that they can deal more damage to them.
In case you need more waveclear sometimes, this Talent helps a bit.
That said, Impale should not be wasted to damage Minions if there are enemy
Heroes around, as it is a key Ability for Anub'arak.
For higher level of play, it is useful to know that the damage component
of this Talent provides vision while happening. Because of this,
you can use Impale in a bush and have vision
there for about 4 seconds, rather than losing it almost instantly.
?

(Level 4)
Anub'arak
Harden Carapace grants 30% increased Movement Speed for 3 seconds.
Shed Exoskeleton is a strong Talent that
provides Anub'arak with a strong and reliable Movement Speed
increase effect that makes up for the lack of mobility
right after using Burrow Charge.
Being based on Harden Carapace,
this Talent has synergy with Chitinous Plating at Level 7
which provides cooldown reduction for it.
?
Underking
(Level 4)
Anub'arak
Increases Burrow Charge range by 20% and damage by 100%.
Underking is a strong Talent that increases both range and damage
of Burrow Charge.
The range increase is great when you want to dive
the enemy backline or when you want to escape.
The extra damage is always welcome, especially if your team wants to
burst down enemy Heroes as fast as possible.

talent_pages.title: Level 7 Talents for Anub'arak
talent_pages.text:
?
Chitinous Plating
(Level 7)
Anub'arak
While Harden Carapace is active, taking damage from enemy Abilities reduces its cooldown by 1 second, up to 3 seconds.
Chitinous Plating is a good Talent that has
the potential of nearly halving the cooldown of
Harden Carapace. This translates into more survivability, more Beetles,
and, later on, more damage, through Urticating Spines at Level 13.
?
Subterranean Shield
(Level 7)
Anub'arak
Burrow Charge also grants a 400 (+4% per level) point Shield for 5 seconds.
Subterranean Shield is a strong Talent that
provides Anub'arak with a substantial survivability
increase that is conveniently located on his main initiation tool.
Subterranean Shield becomes particularly potent when combined with
Epicenter at Level 16.
✔
Leeching Scarabs
(Level 7)
Anub'arak
Beetles attacks deal 30% more damage and heal Anub'arak 50% of damage dealt if he is nearby.
Leeching Scarabs is a good Talent that offers
a nice amount of self-sustain and a bit more damage, however,
it requires Legion of Beetles at Level 1
and gets better when combined with Beetle, Juiced at Level 16.

talent_pages.title: Level 10 Talents for Anub'arak
talent_pages.text:
In this section we discuss when and why to pick a given Heroic Ability.
If you want to read how they work in detail and/or you are looking for some tips on how to use them,
check them out on the Abilities and Strategy page.
?
Locust Swarm
(Level 10)
Anub'arak
Mana: 75
Cooldown: 100 seconds
Deal 68 (+4% per level) damage per second to nearby enemies. Each enemy damaged restores 24 (+4% per level) Health. Lasts 6 seconds.
Locust Swarm is a good Heroic Ability that makes Anub'arak extremely difficult to
take out for its duration, on top of making him impossible to ignore due to the
Ability's sheer area of effect damage output.
You should pick this Heroic Ability
only if you expect to not get any value from Cocoon,
such as when the enemy team has multiple tools to blow it up immediately
and you cannot block them in the way explained below.
For beginners, we recommend selecting Locust Swarm
as Heroic Ability because it increases your survivability and damage output.
If you are confident with using Cocoon, then go for it.
✔
Cocoon
(Level 10)
Anub'arak
Mana: 70
Cooldown: 70 seconds
Wraps target enemy Hero in a cocoon, rendering them unable to act or be targeted for 7 seconds. Allies of the Hero can attack the cocoon to break it and free them early.
Cocoon is a strong Heroic Ability that can be used to get
numerical advantage for a few seconds, usually enough to secure a kill.
Keep in mind that enemy Heroes who are Unstoppable
are invalid targets. If the projectile is already flying towards them
while they become Unstoppable, then
Cocoon will be wasted and go on full cooldown.
Use Cocoon on Heroes who
possess tools to destroy it in less than 2-3 seconds.
Alternatively, engage them so that
they cannot break it immediately due to being unable to act.
If these tips cannot be applied to the game you are playing,
then consider picking Locust Swarm instead.

talent_pages.title: Level 13 Talents for Anub'arak
talent_pages.text:
?
Urticating Spines
(Level 13)
Anub'arak
Casting Harden Carapace will also deal 90 (+4% per level) damage to nearby enemies. Deals double damage against Heroes.
Urticating Spines is a good Talent
that deals a high amount of burst damage to enemy Heroes
near Anub'arak when Harden Carapace gets used.
The damage done via this Talent counts as Spell Damage.
✔
Burning Beetles
(Level 13)
Anub'arak
Deal 21 (+4% per level) damage per second to nearby enemies. Beetles deal 6 (+4% per level) damage per second to nearby enemies.
Burning Beetles is a strong Talent that provides
a lot of sustain damage when combined
with some Scarab Host-related Talents:
Legion of Beetles at Level 1 and Beetle, Juiced at Level 16.
The damage done via this Talent counts as Spell Damage.
✘
Acid-Drenched Mandibles
(Level 13)
Anub'arak
Attacking a Hero that is Slowed, Rooted, or Stunned increases Anub'arak's Basic Attack damage by 80% for 4 seconds.
Acid-Drenched Mandibles is a weak Talent that
provides a good amount of sustain damage,
in the form of Physical Damage, against enemy Heroes recently affected
by specific crowd control effects:
Slow, Root, and Stun.
We do not recommend this Talent because its damage is too low compared to the alternatives in the same Tier:
Urticating Spines when you need burst damage
and Burning Beetles when you need sustain damage.

talent_pages.title: Level 16 Talents for Anub'arak
talent_pages.text:
✔
Epicenter
(Level 16)
Anub'arak
Increases Burrow Charge impact area by 60% and lowers the cooldown by 1 second for each Hero hit.
Epicenter is a strong Talent that primarily helps
you land Burrow Charge on enemy Heroes
while also reducing its cooldown when it successfully hits them.
We find this Talent great when you are allowed to play Anub'arak aggressively,
to dive the enemy backline together with
allied Heroes or with their follow-up from afar.
Being tied to your only escape,
this Talent should not be picked when you definitely cannot afford
to use Burrow Charge aggressively
(for example against Garrosh).
?
Debilitation
(Level 16)
Anub'arak
Enemy Heroes hit by Burrow Charge or Impale have their Spell Power reduced by 50% for 4 seconds.
Debilitation is a situational Talent
that reduces the Spell Power of enemy Heroes
recently hit with Impale or Burrow Charge,
halving all the damage and healing they deal with their Abilities.
You can use this Talent to deal with powerful Healers
(such as Whitemane) and/or to reduce the self-healing of certain Heroes
(for example W Build Diablo), so that they cannot get value
from their Abilities when your Stuns end
and they are not dead yet.
?
Beetle, Juiced
(Level 16)
Anub'arak
Passive: Beetles gain 30% increased health.
Every 4th Basic Attack spawns a Beetle.
Beetle, Juiced is a good Talent that increases
the survivability of your Beetles and makes Scarab Host
spawn a Beetle once every 4 Basic Attacks. The spawning effect works when attacking
non-Heroes too, so it can be used to tank additional shots of enemy Structures
while pushing with your team.
Since it occasionally spawns additional Beetles and makes them harder to kill, this Talent
has synergy with any Scarab Host-related Talent:
Legion of Beetles at Level 1, Leeching Scarabs at Level 7,
and Burning Beetles at Level 13.
Do not pick this Talent without other Beetle-based Talents.

talent_pages.title: Level 20 Talents for Anub'arak
talent_pages.text:
?
Hive Master
(Level 20)
Anub'arak
Gain a permanent Vampire Locust that attacks a nearby enemy every 3 seconds. The Vampire Locust deals 165 (+4% per level) damage and returns to heal Anub'arak for 80 (+4% per level) health.
Hive Master is a decent Talent that
gives you a permanent Vampire Locust which deals damage to a single nearby enemy
once every 3 seconds and heals Anub'arak for about half of that amount.
The self-sustain
and sustain damage provided by this Talent
are designed for long team fights. Unless in ARAM, we do not recommend
this Talent because Rewind offers more playmaking
potential together with additional survivability and more damage.
?
Cryptweave
(Level 20)
Anub'arak
Staying near the Cocoon allows Anub'arak to extend the duration by up to 6 seconds per Cocoon. Upon exiting the Cocoon, enemies take 60 (+4% per level) damage over 4 seconds. This damage is increased by 100% for each second that they were inside.
Cryptweave is a situational Talent that can extend
the duration of Cocoon, but only if Anub'arak stays within 4.5 range.
In addition to that, the targeted Hero will take damage based on how long it lasted.
You can occasionally use this Talent against scary enemy Heroes (notably Cho)
to keep them blocked while fighting the rest of their team
and at the same time dealing a moderate amount of damage to them.
?
The Traitor King
(Level 20)
Anub'arak
Cooldown: 60 seconds
Gain 10% bonus maximum Health and 20 Spell Armor.
Activate to gain 75 Armor for 4 seconds.
The Traitor King is a situational Talent that passively gives
Anub'arak 10% additional maximum Health and 20 Spell Armor,
and it can also be activated once every 60 seconds to gain 75 Armor for a few seconds.
The huge amount of survivability provided by this Talent makes Anub'arak
way harder to kill with burst damage. That said,
you will rarely need this Talent instead of Rewind.
✔
Rewind
(Level 20)
Anub'arak
Cooldown: 60 seconds
Activate to reset the cooldowns of your Basic Abilities.
Rewind is a strong Talent that allows Anub'arak
to instantly reset the cooldown of all his Basic Abilities once every 60 seconds.
The effect provided is outstanding and versatile, allowing you to double your
burst damage, survivability, and crowd control on demand.
Being able to cast Impale
and Burrow Charge twice in a row can lead to some of
the game's longest crowd control chains.
Thanks to Scarab Host, you will be also summoning 3 additional Beetles to assist you,
effectively increasing your damage output.
Make sure that you have used most if not all your Basic Abilities
before using Rewind, else you will waste part or all of its effect.
